en.headline: Government proposes HK$6 per kg levy on EV battery suppliers from 2028
en.dek: The Environmental Protection Department said the charge would start at about HK$3,000 for a typical private car battery and rise to about HK$15,000 by 2043.
body: The Environmental Protection Department said on Friday that Hong Kong plans to impose a recycling levy of HK$6 per kilogram on electric vehicle battery suppliers from 2028 under a proposed producer responsibility scheme.

For a typical private car with a 500 kg battery, the initial charge would be about HK$3,000, rising by about HK$800 a year to reach about HK$15,000 in 2043. The department said market forces would determine whether suppliers pass the costs to owners.

Retired batteries are expected to grow from about 1,300 tonnes this year to about 6,700 tonnes by 2030. More than 180,000 existing EVs would be exempt from the levy but still receive one free recycling service when the battery is replaced or the vehicle is scrapped.
The government aims to submit amendments to the Legislative Council in 2027, with a preparatory phase in 2028 and full implementation targeted for 2029.

zh.headline: 政府擬向電動車電池供應商徵費每公斤6元 料2028年起實施
zh.dek: 環保署表示，一般私家車約500公斤電池初期徵費約3000元，至2043年逐步增至約15000元。
body: 環境保護署周五表示，政府計劃於2028年起推行電動車電池生產者責任計劃，向供應商按電池重量徵收循環再造徵費，起始水平為每公斤6元。
以一般私家車配備約500公斤電池計算，初期收費約3000元，其後每年增加約800元，至2043年增至約15000元。署方指，供應商會否把費用轉嫁車主，由市場力量決定。
退役電池量預料由今年約1300公噸增至2030年約6700公噸。已在路上的超過18萬輞電動車將獲豁免徵費，但車主在更換電池或報廢車輞時仍可享一次免費回收服務。
政府目標明年向立法會提交修例草案，2028年進入籌備階段，2029年全面推行。
